 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 10-10-2023 at about 05-30 p.m., the petitioner was discharging traffic duty at Nagawara ring road, Near Manyataw Gate No.2, Nagawara, Bangalore.

At that time the driver of Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-03/AK- 7189, drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Baptist Hospital for first aid, then he was shifted to Wockhardt Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.75,000/- towards treatment and other incidental charges.
He has to incur future medical expenses also.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as Assistant Police Sub Inspector, at Hennur Police station, Bangalore and drawing sum of Rs.42,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner had not attended the duty for nearly 61 days and not in a position to do the said work as earlier.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.

4. Respondent no.1/ the insurer of Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-03/AK-7189 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the Cab was not holding valid driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid R.C, Permit and FC as on the date of accident.
It is further contended that the offending Cab is not at all involved in the accident and the said vehicle was falsely implicated for unlawful gains.
It is further contended that accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself.
5. Respondent no.2/

the RC owner of the Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-03/AK-7189 has filed written statement and contended that he is the owner of the said vehicle and same was insured with the 1 st respondent and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

He further contended that the driver of his vehicle was holding valid driving licence and alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of his vehicle.

Further contended that, the petitioner is not entitled to claim any interest on non pecuniary Rajanna T vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28285813/
2 damages as per the observation of Hon'ble Apex court.

sentences.text:
6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that On 10- 10-2023 at about 5-30 p.m. when he was traffic duty near Nagawar ring road, Manyatha gate No.2,
Nagawara, Bangalore at that time the driver of Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-03/AK-7189 drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, as a result he fell down and sustained severe injuries, as mentioned in the claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 and closed evidence from his side.
The respondent no.1 and 2 have not adduced their evidence.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, PW.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 10-10-2023 at about 05-30 p.m., when he was discharging traffic duty at Nagawara ring road, near Manyataw Gate No.2, Nagawara, Bangalore, at that time the driver of Cab bearing Reg.No.KA-03/AK-7189 (here in after called the offending vehicle) drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against him, result of which he sustained grievous injuries.

PW.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.
In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 13.

Out of which Ex.P1 to 7 are the police records such as F.I.R, Complaint, Spot Sketch,
Spot mahazar, IMV report, Charge sheet and Wound Certificate.

12. On the basis of the Statement/complaint lodged by petitioner/Rajanna T. case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.154/2023 of Hennur Traffic Police Rajanna T vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28285813/
3 Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of IPC.

After completion of investigation,
the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279 and 337 of IPC.
13.
The respondents have not disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.

The respondent no.1 both in the written statement and evidence has categorically taken the contention that, the petitioner who was busy in controlling the traffic, without observing the offending vehicle negligently came in contact with the offending vehicle, hence the accident in question was due to the sole negligent act on the part of the petitioner.
14. It is not in dispute that, at the time of accident the petitioner was discharging public duty at the spot of accident by controlling the traffic.
It is also not in dispute that barricade was fixed near the spot of accident.
The sketch at Ex.P3 discloses that petitioner was standing in front of the barricade.
The object of fixing barricade is to enhance safety by creating physical barriers that restrict access to hazardous areas or manage traffic flow.

The scene of occurrence as depicted in the spot sketch clearly reveals that, the offending vehicle which came in the said road dashed to the barricade,
proceeded ahead and dashed to the petitioner.
When barricade was fixed on the right side of the road, the driver of the offending vehicle had to take his vehicle on the left side of the road.
But by driving the vehicle on the right side of the road in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the barricade and thereafter to the petitioner.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that the accident in question was due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P7 and P8.

On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 10-10- 2023 to 13-10-2023 at Fortis Hospital,
for a period of 4 days.
As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained two simple injuries.

16. To substantiate that there is loss of income due to the permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, he has not examined any doctor who has got expertise in this field or any evidence in this regard.
He has not placed disability certificate issued by the competent person.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future loss of income.
At the most for the injuries suffered by the petitioner, he may be entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.
17. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two simple injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering.

18. Even though, petitioner has stated that he has taken treatment at Wockhardt Hospital, as inpatient, but there are no materials available to say how many days he took treatment as an inpatient and what kind of treatment he has taken for the injuries sustained in the accident in the Rajanna T vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 1 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28285813/
4 said hospital.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However he has produced one discharge summary issued by Fortis hospital, which is marked as Ex.P8, which discloses that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient in the said hospital from 10-10-2023 to 13-10-2023 i.e., for 4 days.

So, the petitioner requires an attendant, was traveled to hospitals for treatment, for follow-ups has incurred traveling expenses, he has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.20,000/-.
19.
Regarding treatment and medical expenses incurred etc, the petitioner has taken treatment at Fortis Hospital, Bangalore.
To that effect he has produced medical bills for Rs.7,690/- at Ex.P11.
The petitioner has not produced inpatient bill.
The medical bills at Ex.P11 produced by the petitioner are for the treatment taken as out patient.
It appears that, the inpatient medical expenses incurred by the petitioner are reimbursed from the department of the petitioner.

If medical bills at Ex.P11 is calculated, it comes around Rs.7,690/- Hence, Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.7,690/-.
20.

It is submitted by the petitioner that at the time of accident, he was aged about 52 years and he was Assistant Sub Inspector by profession and drawing salary of Rs.42,000/- p.m. and after the accident he could not attend his work for 61 days.
But to prove the same he has not produced any document and he has not examined his employer.
Herein this case, the petitioner is working as Police Sub Inspector and in their department there is E.L. (earned leave) facility.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of income during laid up period.

21. The petitioner at his age of 52 years has suffered injuries as shown in the wound certificate,
which may have caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.50,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000-00  2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000-00  charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges  3. Medical expenses Rs. 7,690-00  4. Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 50,000-00
Total Rs
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,07,690/- (Rupees one lakh seven thousand Six hundred and ninety only).

sentences.text: As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 1 st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no.1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered.
23. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.1,07,690/- (Rupees One Lakh Seven Thousand Six Hundred Ninety only) interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit of the said amount and interest, entire compensation amount shall be released to the petitioner through E- payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 1st day of August 2025)
(ROOPASHRI) XXII Addl. SCJ & ACJM Bengaluru.
